A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Slo2 channel function depends on SCYL1 protein, which is produced in a RNA editing-dependent manner.
SCYL1 is a positive regulator of Slo2 function and its expression is regulated by ADR-1/SCYE1 through RNA editing.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the function of Slo2 channels is regulated by RNA editing of scyl- 1.
RNA editing of a single adenosines in scyl-2 mRNA 3’-untranslated region is essential for the regulation of SLO-2 channel function by SCYL-1.
